==English== ===Alternative forms=== * {{alter|en|sence}} {{q|archaic}} ===Etymology=== {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:sense|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|sense}}, from {{der|en|fro|[[sens]], [[sen]], [[san]]|t=sense, perception, direction}}; partly from {{der|en|la|sēnsus|t=sensation, feeling, meaning}}, from {{m|la|sentiō|t=feel, perceive}}; partly of {{der|en|gem}} origin (whence also {{cog|oc|sen}}, {{cog|it|senno}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|*sennus|t=sense, reason, way}}, from {{der|en|frk|*sinn}} {{gl|"reason, judgement, mental faculty, way, direction"; whence also {{cog|nl|zin}}, {{cog|de|Sinn}}, {{cog|sv|sinne}}, {{cog|no|sinn}}}}. Both Latin and Germanic from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sent-|t=to feel}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|sĕns}}, {{IPA|en|/sɛns/|/sɛnts/}} * {{audio|en|En-us-sense.ogg|a=GA}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Back ache-sense.wav|a=UK}} * {{IPA|en|/sɪns/|/sɪnts/|a=pin-pen}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛns|s=1}} * {{homophones|en|cents|scents|;|since}} ===Noun=== {{wikidata lexeme|L18025}} {{en-noun|~}} {{wp|,Word +}} # {{senseid|en|manner to perceive}} Any of the manners by which living beings [[perceive]] the physical world: for humans [[sight]], [[smell]], [[hearing]], [[touch]], [[taste]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Twelfth Night|IV|i|passage=Let fancy still my '''sense''' in Lethe steep.}} #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=V|passage=What surmounts the reach / Of human '''sense''' I shall delineate.|year=1873}} #* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:National Geographic|year=1987|month=October|volume=172|number=4|title=Results of the Smell Survey|author=Avery N. Gilbert and Charles J. Wysocki|page=514 |text=Sight, hearing, and touch have been well explored, but the '''sense''' of smell has remained elusive, due in large measure to a lack of basic information.}} # {{senseid|en|conscious awareness}}Perception through the intellect; [[apprehension]]; [[awareness]]. #: {{ux|en|a '''sense''' of security}} #* {{RQ:Sidney Arcadia|passage=this Basilius, having the quick '''sense''' of a lover}} #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=I|passage=high disdain from '''sense''' of injured merit|year=1873}} #* {{RQ:Tennyson In Memoriam|XLIII|66|The days have vanish’d, tone and tint,
⁠And yet perhaps the hoarding '''sense'''
⁠Gives out at times (he knows not whence)
A little flash, a mystic hint; {{...}}}} # {{senseid|en|sound judgment}} Sound practical or moral [[judgment]]. #: {{ux|en|It’s common '''sense''' not to put metal objects in a microwave oven.}} #* {{RQ:L'Estrange Fables of Aesop|passage=some People so Harden'd in Wickedness, as to have No Sense at all of the most Friendly Offices, or the Highest Benefits.}} # {{senseid|en|meaning or reason, generally}} The [[meaning]], [[reason]], or [[value]] of something. #: {{ux|en|You don’t make any '''sense'''.}} #: {{ux|en|That just don't make a licka '''sense''' to me.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Taming of the Shrew|I|i|passage=I think ’twas in another '''sense'''.}} ## {{senseid|en|any particular meaning of a word}} A meaning of a [[term]] ([[word]] or [[expression]]), among its various meanings. ##: {{hypo|en|subsense|subsubsense}} ##: {{ux|en|the various '''senses''' of the word “car” (e.g., motor car, elevator car, railcar)}} ## {{senseid|en|semantics term}} {{lb|en|semantics|lexicography}} A single conventional use of a word; one of the [[entry#Noun|entries]] or [[definition]]s for a word in a dictionary. # {{senseid|en|natural ability}} A natural [[appreciation]] or [[ability]]. #: {{ux|en|A keen musical '''sense'''}} # {{senseid|en|pragmatics term}}{{lb|en|pragmatics}} The way that a [[referent]] is presented. # {{senseid|en|math: direction of a vector}}{{lb|en|mathematics}} One of two opposite directions in which a vector (especially of motion) may point. See also [[polarity]]. # {{senseid|en|math: direction of rotation}}{{lb|en|mathematics}} One of two opposite directions of rotation, [[clockwise]] versus [[anti-clockwise]]. #
